summary: R-9: a lens's record is stale only when a file whose kinds select that lens moved since the record. `lens record` stores a snapshot of the review-scope files and their content keys; `lens_staleness` compares it with the tree at check time and asks `_file_kinds` (extracted from `detect_change_kinds`, one function for the plan and for staleness) which kinds moved; the always-on lens is stale on any move, a record without a snapshot on any digest change. `lens plan` prints `stale` (why) and `run` (missing plus stale); `check_reviews`, `next` and the workflow use it. A file under skills/, .agents/, agents/ or hooks/ is code whatever its suffix, and its prose is not scanned for hints (the framework's own materialised copies contain the word 'session'). R-10: the doc-sync protocol has a verification pass and the doc-manager attests under its own name with a note; no step waits for a person to attest. The SPEC-2 architecture preamble names the deleted contracts. Round 1 (three lenses): three blocking findings fixed — a record now also stores the kinds each file carried when the lens read it, so a control deleted afterwards stales the lens that read it; a moved contract file under .aegis/ re-takes every review; source under agents/ or hooks/ is scanned again and only protocol .md files are code-unscanned. The preamble names R-4 and the snapshot; the workflow's first round dispatches `run`; README says what invalidates a review now. Round 2: the plan's staleness loop now covers recorded lenses the diff no longer selects (a deleted, committed control), so `run` says what the gate demands; the task's own manifest is keyed by its contract half in the snapshot, as the digest keys it, so the gate's status write stales nothing; the preamble names the stored kinds. Round 3 (the cap): all three lenses pass.
